newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot LPGs mixed as crude weakens.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot LPGs mixed as crude weakens.

text.p: U.S. spot LPG prices were mixed in late trade on Wednesday as speculation over demand propped up Midwest prices but weakening crude oil futures put the lid on the U.S. Gulf Coast.
Spot propane prices in both hubs skyrocketed about 2.25 cents in early trade, fueled by firm NYMEX November crude oil futures in early dealings.
November crude oil eventually ended down 9 cents a barrel, bringing down Mont Belvieu, Texas.
Traders said Belvieu spot propane dipped 0.25 cent in late trade to between 50.50 cents and 50.75 cents a gallon.
Conway, Kansas, material remained firm at 51.50/51.75 cents, due to speculation of an early, wet harvest because of a crop-killer freeze entering the region.
Farmers use propane to dry their corn crops before putting them in storage.
In other liquids, Belvieu normal butane traded at 52.00 cents, a half cent higher than at midday. Conway material also edged up 0.25 cent in thin talk.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
